newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Pacific BBA to spend A$20mln on Asia plants.
newsitem.headline: Pacific BBA to spend A$20mln on Asia plants.

text.p: Manufacturing group Pacific BBA Ltd said on Wednesday it would spend about A$20 million on two new Webforge construction products plants planned for China and Thailand.
Managing director Barry Jackson said the Chinese plant, Webforge's second in China, would be completed by mid-1998, and the plant in Thailand would be commissioned in the second quarter of 1998.
Pacific BBA's Webforge subsidiary makes steel and aluminium gratings and tubular handrails.
In China, Pacific BBA said agreement had been reached for a joint venture, owned 75 percent by Pacific BBA and 25 percent by Wuxi No.3 Iron & Steel Co Ltd, for a plant west of Shanghai at Wuxi.
In Thailand, Webforge had acquired land near Bangkok and construction would start soon.
The project followed Pacific BBA's acquisition of Webforge's local distributor Traflo Ltd earlier this year, the company said.
"We will continue to expand our presence in Asia in order to service the growing markets and many new infrastructure projects throughout the region," Jackson said in a statement.
Webforge has manufacturing facilities in Australia, New Zealand, China, Indonesia, Singapore and the Philippines.
Plans for the two new plants were announced at Pacific BBA's annual general meeting on April 30.
